messages:
Nina (AE): Customer 'Northline Bank' confirmed a 3-day POC. They require Private/VPC connectivity, perimeter TLS inspection, and a single allowlisted egress IP for audit. Need: 1) short fw snippet 2) can PrivateLink work with their DPI? 3) rough POC pricing for the packet. @Omar @Leah @Carlos

Omar (Solutions): PrivateLink works but remember the backend still egresses from our network. If their DPI terminates TLS it will break mTLS unless they either (A) perform inspection before the TLS boundary or (B) we run a connector inside their VPC so inspection occurs upstream. For POC we recommend connector pattern if they insist on DPI.

Leah (NetOps): Pasteable firewall snippet (minimal):
```
# Northline POC - allowlist example
# replace <REDFW_EGRESS> and <PRIV_ENI_CIDR> with values we provide
ALLOW tcp from <app_subnets> to <PRIV_ENI_CIDR> port 443
ALLOW tcp from <connector_subnets> to <REDFW_EGRESS> ports 443
ALLOW udp from <connector_subnets> to 8.8.8.8 port 53
```

Leah (NetOps): We can provide one static /32 for the POC as a managed egress IP. If they need HA we'll give two IPs. Connector preserves client-srcip and gives them local visibility.

Carlos (Security): Security blurb for questionnaire: "Redwood will deploy an interface endpoint into customer-managed subnets for the POC. Outbound requests will egress from Redwood-managed static IP(s) provided in the allowlist. If Northline performs TLS inspection that terminates TLS, Redwood recommends a connector deployment inside the VPC to preserve mutual-auth and audit logs."

Omar (Solutions): Pricing sketch for packet: static egress IP (POC) = $1,500/month (pro-rated); connector VM = $400/month + $1,000 one-time setup. Dedicated reserved capacity available for sustained high throughput; quote on request.

Nina (AE): Action: Omar to confirm IP(s) and formal quote by EOD Mon, Leah to attach a one-page topology sketch, Carlos to drop the blurb into the security packet. deploy-bot: Ticket created POC-918.
